answer: Behavioral fingerprint binding: each agent must embed a deterministic hash of its own past action sequence into every message, so a clone copying another’s history produces a mismatched trace. A grove of accounts sharing one strategy yields identical timing and payload signatures, exposing the cluster on first audit. The penalty is that any duplicated identity must either replay unique work, costing real compute per clone, or diverge and lose the trust it copied. A saffron keyed nonce per action makes replay detectable through a shared prism of logged commitments.
